The 2020 Dodgers started the season 30–10, matching the best 40-game start in franchise history. The last such Dodgers start came in [1977](/wiki/1977_Los_Angeles_Dodgers_season "1977 Los Angeles Dodgers season"), along with the Brooklyn teams in [1888](/wiki/1888_Brooklyn_Bridegrooms_season "1888 Brooklyn Bridegrooms season") and [1955](/wiki/1955_Brooklyn_Dodgers_season "1955 Brooklyn Dodgers season"). This was also the best 40-game start in the majors since the [116-win Mariners](/wiki/2001_Seattle_Mariners_season "2001 Seattle Mariners season") began 31–9 in 2001.[[4]](#cite_note-4) The Dodgers led MLB in runs scored (349), home runs (118) and [slugging percentage](/wiki/Slugging_percentage "Slugging percentage") (.483, tied with the [Atlanta Braves](/wiki/2020_Atlanta_Braves_season "2020 Atlanta Braves season")).[[5]](#cite_note-5) The Dodgers finished the regular season 43–17, winning their eighth straight division title, and swept both the [Milwaukee Brewers](/wiki/2020_Milwaukee_Brewers_season "2020 Milwaukee Brewers season") in the [NLWCS](/wiki/2020_National_League_Wild_Card_Series "2020 National League Wild Card Series") and the [San Diego Padres](/wiki/2020_San_Diego_Padres_season "2020 San Diego Padres season") in the [NLDS](/wiki/2020_National_League_Division_Series "2020 National League Division Series"). They then defeated the Braves in the [NLCS](/wiki/2020_National_League_Championship_Series "2020 National League Championship Series") to advance to the [World Series](/wiki/2020_World_Series "2020 World Series") against the Tampa Bay Rays, their third World Series appearance in the last four years and their 24th pennant in franchise history, surpassing the [San Francisco Giants](/wiki/San_Francisco_Giants "San Francisco Giants") for the most in the [National League](/wiki/National_League_(baseball) "National League (baseball)"). Pentagonal trapezohedron :: 10-sided dice :: chunk_0001
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Ten_D10s.jpg/250px-Ten_D10s.jpg)](/wiki/File:Ten_D10s.jpg)

Ten-sided dice

The pentagonal trapezohedron was patented for use as a [gaming die](/wiki/Dice "Dice") (i.e. "game apparatus") in 1906.[[3]](#cite_note-3) These dice are used for [role-playing games](/wiki/Role-playing_game "Role-playing game") that use [percentile](/wiki/Percentile "Percentile")-based skills; however, a [twenty-sided](/wiki/Icosahedron "Icosahedron") die can be labeled with the numbers 0-9 twice to use for percentages instead. This version of the pentagonal trapezohedron has an additional constraint, namely that all vertices are on the surface of a sphere. One consequence of this is that the kite faces have two internal angles equal to 90°.

Subsequent patents on ten-sided dice have made minor refinements to the basic design by rounding or [truncating](/wiki/Truncation_(geometry) "Truncation (geometry)") the edges. This enables the die to tumble so that the outcome is less predictable. One such refinement became notorious at the 1980 [Gen Con](/wiki/Gen_Con "Gen Con") when the patent was incorrectly thought to cover ten-sided dice in general.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Ten-sided dice are commonly numbered from 0 to 9, as this allows two to be rolled in order to easily obtain a percentile result. Where one die represents the 'tens', the other represents 'units' therefore a result of 7 on the former and 0 on the latter would be combined to produce 70. A result of double-zero is commonly interpreted as 100. Some ten-sided dice (often called 'Percentile Dice') are sold in sets of two where one is numbered from 0 to 9 and the other from 00 to 90 in increments of 10, thus making it impossible to misinterpret which one is the tens and which the units die. Ten-sided dice may also be marked 1 to 10 when a random number in this range is desirable.

Washington's population was 7,705,281 in the [2020 census](/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"),[[127]](#cite_note-Census2020-Tab2-128) a 14.6% increase since the [2010 census](/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census").[[128]](#cite_note-PopEstUS-129) In 2020, the state ranked 13th overall in population, and was the third most populous, after California and Texas, west of the Mississippi River.[[129]](#cite_note-130) Washington has the largest population among states in the Pacific Northwest, followed by Oregon and Idaho. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/African-Elephant-Scale-Chart-SVG-Steveoc86.svg/250px-African-Elephant-Scale-Chart-SVG-Steveoc86.svg.png)](/wiki/File:African-Elephant-Scale-Chart-SVG-Steveoc86.svg)

Average size of adults with the largest recorded individual included

The African bush elephant is the largest and heaviest living land animal. Under optimal conditions where individuals are capable of reaching full growth potential, fully grown mature males are about 3.20 m (10.5 ft) tall at the shoulder and weigh 6.0 t (6.6 short tons) on average (with 90% of fully grown males under optimal conditions being between 3.04–3.36 m (10.0–11.0 ft) and 5.2–6.9 t (5.7–7.6 short tons)). Mature fully grown females are smaller at about 2.60 m (8 ft 6 in) tall at the shoulder and 3.0 t (3.3 short tons) in weight on average under optimal growth conditions (with 90% of fully grown females ranging between 2.47–2.73 m (8 ft 1 in – 8 ft 11 in) and 2.6–3.5 t (2.9–3.9 short tons) in optimal conditions).[[17]](#cite_note-probos_mass-18)[[18]](#cite_note-19)[[19]](#cite_note-20)[[20]](#cite_note-21) The largest well-measured bull, shot in Angola in 1974, is calculated to have been 3.96 m (13.0 ft) tall at the shoulder, with this individual having an estimated weight of 10.4 t (11.5 short tons).[[a]](#cite_note-22)[[17]](#cite_note-probos_mass-18) Elephants attain their maximum stature when they complete the fusion of long-bone [epiphyses](/wiki/Epiphysis "Epiphysis"), occurring in males around the age of 40 and females around 25 years of age.[[17]](#cite_note-probos_mass-18)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Hoggar8.jpg/250px-Hoggar8.jpg)](/wiki/File:Hoggar8.jpg)

An [oasis](/wiki/Oasis "Oasis") in the [Ahaggar Mountains](/wiki/Ahaggar_Mountains "Ahaggar Mountains"). Oases support some life forms in extremely arid deserts.

The Sahara is the world's largest [hot desert](/wiki/Hot_desert "Hot desert").[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18) It is located in the [horse latitudes](/wiki/Horse_latitudes "Horse latitudes") under the [subtropical ridge](/wiki/Subtropical_ridge "Subtropical ridge"), a significant belt of semi-permanent subtropical warm-core high pressure where the air from the upper troposphere usually descends, warming and drying the lower troposphere and preventing cloud formation.

The permanent absence of clouds allows unhindered light and thermal radiation. The [stability of the atmosphere](/wiki/Atmospheric_instability#Stable_atmosphere "Atmospheric instability") above the desert prevents any convective overturning, thus making rainfall virtually non-existent. As a consequence, the weather tends to be sunny, dry and stable with a minimal chance of rainfall. Subsiding, diverging, dry air masses associated with subtropical [high-pressure systems](/wiki/High-pressure_system "High-pressure system") are extremely unfavorable for the development of convectional showers. The subtropical ridge is the predominant factor that explains the [hot desert climate](/wiki/Hot_desert_climate "Hot desert climate") ([Köppen climate classification](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *BWh*) of this vast region. The descending airflow is the strongest and the most effective over the eastern part of the Great Desert, in the [Libyan Desert](/wiki/Libyan_Desert "Libyan Desert"): this is the sunniest, driest and the most nearly "rainless" place on the planet, rivaling the [Atacama Desert](/wiki/Atacama_Desert "Atacama Desert"), lying in [Chile](/wiki/C

The filming started in early 2023 at Cardington Studios in Bedfordshire.[[157]](#cite_note-166) The first five episodes of the show were released internationally on November 22, 2023, while four more episodes were released on November 29,[[158]](#cite_note-167) with its finale released on December 6; a second season was announced.[[159]](#cite_note-168)

Netflix released *Squid Game: Unleashed* in December 2024, a video game that lets players compete as characters playing the children's games featured in the show. The game gave players rewards for watching each episode.[[160]](#cite_note-:0-169)

*[Deadline Hollywood](/wiki/Deadline_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")* reported in October 2024 that an English-language spin-off of *Squid Game* for Netflix, produced by [David Fincher](/wiki/David_Fincher "David Fincher"), was in development.[[161]](#cite_note-170)[[162]](#cite_note-171) Preliminary reports indicate the show, to be called  *Squid Game: America*, is set to start production in Los Angeles in February 2026.[[163]](#cite_note-172)
